headline: Congress cancels a 2023 order that had blocked mineral and geothermal leasing on about 225,504 acres of national forest in northeastern Minnesota.
what_it_does: This law overturns Public Land Order 7917, a Bureau of Land Management rule from 2023. That order had closed about 225,504 acres of National Forest land in Cook, Lake, and Saint Louis Counties to mineral and geothermal leasing for 20 years. The order was meant to protect the Rainy River Watershed, the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness and its nearby Mining Protection Area, and the 1854 Ceded Territory of the Lake Superior Chippewa. With the order cancelled, the land can again be leased for mineral and geothermal exploration and development.

who_it_affects.how: They can now seek federal leases to explore for and develop minerals and geothermal energy on these lands.
Land in the 1854 Ceded Territory that had been shielded from mineral and geothermal leasing is no longer protected by the cancelled order.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of Cook, Lake, and Saint Louis Counties, Minnesota
who_it_affects.how: National Forest land in their area is reopened to possible mineral and geothermal leasing and development.

who_it_affects.group: Visitors to the Boundary Waters Canoe Area Wilderness
who_it_affects.how: Nearby lands in the Rainy River Watershed and the Mining Protection Area lose the leasing protections the 2023 order had put in place.

when_it_takes_effect: April 27, 2026, when the law was enacted.
